scope: Theorem 5.1 of the manuscript “Slope-field perturbations of the two-cylinder covering” (preprints/Slope-field-perturbations-of-the-two-cylinder-covering-September-27-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 100 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 6e6336ef3860f900), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 11-12. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every 1 < p < ( √ 51 − 5)/2, 1 < γ < 1/(2 − p), all sufficiently small positive c determine a finite cylinder cover of the regular edge-2 tetrahedron K2 above with total perpendicular base area less than √ 2/2. The cover consists of two finite families with compact parallelogram bases and two cylinders with compact triangular bases. Before the arbitrarily small errors needed for the two finite approximations, the area bound is √ 2 2 + 2 √ 2 κpc2 + o(c2 ), κp = (1/2)4(2p2 + 10p − 13) 30p < 0. 11 The asymptotic statement fixes p and γ first. Each finite approximation is chosen after the positive value of c is fixed.
